newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada supplies Japan's growing appetite for beef.
newsitem.headline: Canada supplies Japan's growing appetite for beef.

text.p: Japan's growing apetite for beef opened the door to more imports from Canadian beef packers who increased output in 1997, analysts said.
"How many sizable markets are doubling their consumption of beef," Agriculture Canada's analyst John Ross said.
Japanese per capita beef consumption rose 90 percent to 11.8 kg in 1995 from 6.2 kg in 1991, Ag Canada figures show.
Japan's beef imports dropped off in calendar 1996 because of a bacterial outbreak and fears of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) problem in the U.K.
Japan continued to import less beef from Jan 1 to April 30, down 4.4 percent on lingering food safety fears, Japan Agriculture and Livestock Industries Corp said.

Australia and U.S. hold the lion's share of Japan's beef import market at 89 percent in the first four months of 1997, but their shipments were down 18.4 and 21.3 percent, respectively, from the same period in 1996, statistics show.
Canada's exports, however, rose 77.7 percent in that time, according to Canada Beef Export Federation statistics.
"We're talking large gains off small amounts but it's a big rise since 1991 and 1992," Ag Canada's Ross said.

Canadian beef exports to Japan rose at 12 percent in each of those years but saw a 40 percent increase in 1995 with a gain of 21 percent in 1996 at 14,226 tonnes versus 11,686 tonnes in 1995 despite the bacterial and BSE fears in Japan, Canada Beef Export Federation figures show.
"We've got our shelf life straightened out, we're keeping it clean and cold," Ross said.

While Canada took steps to assuage safety concerns, supply was ratched up as well as Alberta, which slaughtered 63 percent of Canada's beef from January 1 to May 24, posted a 14 percent rise in output, Ag Canada statistics show.

"Supply is up, so exports are up as well," CANFAX beef analyst Anne Dunford said. "Exports to the U.S. (Canada's top market) are up and to Asia as well. The Canadian processor deserves a pat on the back."
Cargill Ltd and Iowa Beef Packers Inc expanded their cattle kill plants in High River and Brooks, Alberta, since 1995. Officials were not available for comment.
"I believe that the Canadian cattle and beef industry will reach its target of exporting 75,000 tonnes of beef (C$450 million) to Japan in 2000," CBEF president Jim Graham said.
